issues.legal_issue: An offence that is not compoundable by law cannot be compounded merely because the parties have reached a settlement.
material_facts: The appellants were convicted of an offence under Section 307 IPC.
During the appeal, the parties reached an amicable settlement and sought permission to compound the offence.
issues.conclusion: The request to compound the offence was rejected.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 320 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, offences that are not compoundable cannot be compounded by the parties. A settlement does not permit compounding of such an offence. The Court relied on Ram Lal and Anr. v. State of J & K (1999) 2 SCC 213 and Ishwar Singh v. State of Madhya Pradesh (2008) 15 SCC 667.

predicates.criminal_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal against a criminal conviction.
predicates.conviction_for_noncompoundable_offense: The accused was convicted of an offence that the law does not permit the parties to compound.
predicates.parties_settled: The parties reached a settlement and sought to compound the offence.

issues.definition: When a criminal appeal concerns a conviction for an offence that cannot be compounded, a settlement between the parties does not prevent refusal of their compounding request.

issues.legal_issue: A settlement that cannot support compounding may nevertheless be considered, together with the circumstances of the case, when determining sentence.
material_facts: The parties had settled their dispute, and the Court considered that settlement a sensible step toward ending the controversy and normalising their relationship.
The incident had occurred many years before the appeal was decided, and the parties were related.
The convicted appellants had been in their twenties at the time of the incident and had served a substantial part of their sentences.
The incident had resulted in a cross-case in which members of the complainant party had also been convicted and sentenced.
The convictions were upheld by the lower courts.
issues.conclusion: The Court reduced the appellants' sentences to the periods they had already served, while upholding their convictions.
issues.legal_principle: A settlement cannot make a non-compoundable offence compoundable, but it may be considered when fixing the sentence. The Court relied on Ram Lal and Anr. v. State of J & K (1999) 2 SCC 213 and Ishwar Singh v. State of Madhya Pradesh (2008) 15 SCC 667, in which settlements were considered in relation to sentence despite refusal to permit compounding.

rule.if: criminal_appeal and conviction_upheld and parties_settled and incident_long_past and parties_related and substantial_sentence_served and cross_case_convictions

predicates.criminal_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal against a criminal conviction and sentence.
predicates.conviction_upheld: The conviction remains in place after the appeal is considered.
predicates.parties_settled: The parties reached a settlement of their dispute.
predicates.incident_long_past: A substantial period had elapsed between the incident and the sentencing decision.
predicates.parties_related: The accused and the opposing party were related to one another.
predicates.substantial_sentence_served: The convicted persons had already served a substantial part of their sentences.
predicates.cross_case_convictions: The same incident led to a cross-case in which members of the opposing party were also convicted.

issues.definition: When, in a criminal appeal, the conviction is upheld and the parties have settled, the elapsed time, relationship, sentence already served, and convictions arising from a cross-case can support reducing the sentence to the time already served.
